claim: K14 LIVE (src/ reverted to 18f5734, 2026-08-07) — computeDragCascade auto-locks both cascade participants, recomputeStartTimes leaves anchorStart stale against every startTime it commits, and applyAnchorBasedTiming's locked branch snaps a locked segment back onto that stale anchor. A drag+cascade on one segment followed by an unrelated lock toggle re-times segments outside {dragged, absorbed, toggled}, and a still-locked segment moves anyway.
scenario: drag s1 (absorb s2, both auto-locked), drag s4 (absorb s5, both auto-locked), unlock s2
note: Drift is measured BEFORE the toggle. The baseline locked branch derives startTime from anchorStart, so it closes the drift by moving the segment — the after-reading is 0 because the defect completed, not because it is absent.
